description: Phase 3B. Exercises the `push` rendezvous channel through its full opt-in lifecycle. Day 1 enables the experimental-families gate; day 2 the user opts into push (engine returns 0 because the soak driver runs the keystore profile, not vault); day 4 a synthetic FCM/APNS data-message is delivered through `soak_simulate_push_payload` and the verifier MUST accept it because the sender publisher is pinned in the soak fixture; day 6 a tampered payload is delivered and the verifier MUST reject it (-5). On day 14 the user opts back out and a subsequent simulated push MUST be rejected (-2) because the engine treats opt-out as a hard gate before the verifier even runs. The legacy subscription-url block holds throughout so the distribution-failure invariants are preserved. Note: the vault-profile rejection (-2 from SetPushRendezvousEnabled) is unit-tested at the ABI layer; this scenario is the soak-level proof that an opted-in keystore engine does NOT regress the 30-day in-engine ledger.
